open_points.subject: A09/A10 HTTP request description and approval digest
open_points.text: A10 rule 7: "The headers sent are exactly: `host`, `accept-encoding: identity` ..." and "The `request_digest` is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of that description."
open_points.question: How is the `host` header value derived exactly (default port included or omitted, IPv6 bracket form, IDN/punycode handling), so that `request_digest` is deterministic and stable across restarts/clients?
options: Derive `host` from URL authority exactly as written in `api_base_url`
Normalize to RFC 7230 host form (lowercase host, include non-default port only)
Use the HTTP client's emitted Host header bytes as authoritative
open_points.default_guess: Normalize to RFC 7230 host form and include port only when non-default.

open_points.subject: A08/A09 base URL validity and join semantics
open_points.text: A08 rule 5 accepts an instance `api_base_url` when it is "an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host"; A09 rule 1 defines request URL as "the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path".
open_points.question: Must `api_base_url` with a path/query/fragment be refused, or allowed and concatenated literally?
options: Refuse any `api_base_url` containing query or fragment, allow optional base path
Allow query/fragment and concatenate literally (implementation-defined result)
Allow only origin form (`scheme://host[:port]`) with no path
open_points.default_guess: Refuse query/fragment; allow optional base path and concatenate with declared path.
